I don't mean the sound of it. I mean the part of you that says what you think, out loud, and then lets it stand.

You've felt it go quiet for a long time, and you've called it other things. Mellowing. Picking your battles. Not having the patience for a fuss anymore. I told you most women guess wrong, and this is how they do it. They name what they got tired of, and never what went missing.

The Magician stands at his table with a white wand held straight up in his right hand, his arm all the way up. It's how you'd put your hand up to speak in a room full of people, except he isn't waiting for anybody to call on him.

Your voice worked like that. A thought came into your head and went straight out of your mouth, before you'd checked who might mind. And once it was out, you let it be. You didn't go back over it afterward and sand the corners off. If it turned out you were wrong, you said that too, and nobody came to any harm.

Before them, none of that took any thought. If somebody asked what you'd rather do, you told them. If you thought a thing was wrong, you said so, then got on with your day and slept fine. You could disagree with somebody across a table and still pass them the bread. You got to the end of your own sentences.
